主要内容: A new bill, the Justice for Patients Act, introduced by Rep. Katie Porter, aims to allow patients to sue health insurance companies in federal court. Currently, many health insurance companies include mandatory arbitration clauses in their contracts, which prevent patients from joining class-action lawsuits and limit their ability to seek justice through the court system. Consumer advocates argue that arbitration is less transparent and offers fewer opportunities for appeal. The bill would block health insurance companies from requiring arbitration and allow patients to bring lawsuits or join class-action suits. The Economic Policy Institute found that only 9% of arbitration cases resulted in monetary relief for consumers. The FAIR Act, a more comprehensive bill passed by the House in 2019, was never voted on in the Senate and would eliminate forced arbitration clauses in various cases. Rep. Hank Johnson re-introduced the FAIR Act in February, but it has only an 8% chance of being enacted.
